_about: Ride-hail explainer page (engine/rideshare/build.py), at docs/toronto/<path>/. Built from the small JSON files cities/toronto/rideshare.py writes to cities/toronto/rideshare/ from the City of Toronto's Private Transportation Companies open data (raw/ptc/, gitignored). Ward boundaries: docs/toronto/data/wards.geojson. Words in 'page' can use {tokens} that build.py fills from the numbers (see TOKENS in build.py). Wording rules (claude/rideshare-scouting.md): 'pickups' or 'completed trips', never 'demand'; no 'surge'; drivers are 'logged in across the city', never placed in a ward; no Uber vs Lyft split; 'average wait' is request to driver arrival.

page.title: When Toronto calls an Uber
page.description: Every Uber and Lyft pickup in Toronto, hour by hour and ward by ward: when the city rides, where, how long people wait and how stretched drivers are. From the City of Toronto's ride-hail open data, August 2025 to July 2026.
page.lede: Toronto took {year2025} ride-hail trips in 2025, a record. They don't come evenly. On an average Monday to Thursday, about {perDay_weekday} rides begin each day; on a Friday, {perDay_fri}. Move the clock and switch the day to see where and when.
page.mapNote: Each ward is shaded by pickups in that hour on the chosen day: an average over the year, counted by the hour the trip began. About {noWard} of Toronto pickups are left off the ward map because the City groups small counts together to protect privacy; they're still in the totals.
page.waitNote: Average wait is the time from the request to the driver's arrival, averaged over every completed pickup in that ward and hour. Wards with fewer than {minTrips} pickups in an hour are left grey.
page.chartNote: Pickups per hour across Toronto, Pearson and the rest of the GTA, for each kind of day. Lines start at 4 a.m. because a night out belongs to the day it started.
page.driversLede: The busiest hour for riders isn't the hardest one for drivers. At {wk8} on a weekday, drivers spend only {idle8} of their logged-in time waiting for a request: the city's tightest hour. In the small hours, they wait about {idleNight} of the time.
page.driversNote: Drivers logged in across the city in each hour, from a sample of four months (October, January, April and July). The City publishes driver time city-wide, not by place, so this can't say where idle drivers are. A driver working two apps is counted once.
page.flowsLede: Downtown's three wards trade riders all day. At 1 a.m. on a Saturday night, the busiest trip from one ward to another is Spadina-Fort York to Toronto Centre.
page.yearsLede: Pickups fell by more than half in 2020 and 2021. They passed 2019's level in 2024 and set a record in 2025.
method: The City of Toronto requires ride-hail companies (Uber, Lyft and others licensed as private transportation companies) to report every trip and every stretch of time a driver is available. Since March 2026 the City has published those records as open data, combined across companies and summed by hour and ward.

This page uses every completed trip from August 1, 2025 to July 30, 2026: {trips} of them, including trips that start in the GTA outside Toronto and at Pearson. A day here runs from 4 a.m. to 4 a.m., so a 1 a.m. pickup on Saturday counts as Friday night. Holidays are left out, and each hour shows the average over all days of that kind ({days}).

Pickups are counted in the ward where the trip began and the hour it began. Drivers are counted city-wide: a driver is logged in during an hour if any of it was spent available, heading to a pickup, waiting or on a trip.

What it leaves out: rides that were requested but never completed (the City's cancellation counts changed in January 2026), anything about price surges (the City's data has none), food delivery, taxis and limousines.
page.credits: Data: City of Toronto, Private Transportation Companies open data (Transportation Services). Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Toronto. Ward boundaries: City of Toronto. Analysis and design: Layers.City.
